ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Higuchi Ichiyō — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Ms. Higuchi is a 24-year-old writer with drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis in the nineteenth week of treatment, now in the continuation phase on isoniazid, rifampin and pyridoxine by video-observed therapy, who comes for the preventive visit booked at her first appointment. Her cough and night sweats have gone, she sleeps well, and she has gained 4 kg since intake. The cystitis five weeks ago settled within two days on nitrofurantoin, and the culture grew Escherichia coli susceptible to it. The sputum culture taken at the end of the intensive phase showed no growth after six weeks. She writes about two hours each morning and has finished a new story. Public funding now covers most of her tuberculosis costs, and the social worker helped her arrange to pay her clinic charges in instalments. She has no new concerns. [S]

Cough for about seven weeks with evening fevers, night sweats, poor appetite and weight loss of about 4 kg (about 10 percent) in a woman of 23; chest X-ray with patchy right upper lobe opacities and no cavity; suspected pulmonary tuberculosis; airborne precautions and three sputum specimens for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification and culture
S — Synthetic presenting problem at intake, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit; its timing echoes her documented decline from early 1896 (D).
Pulmonary tuberculosis of the right upper lobe, sputum smear-negative, confirmed by Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra (Mycobacterium tuberculosis detected, low; rifampin resistance not detected)
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented tuberculosis; all bacteriology and imaging are synthetic.

S — Synthetic nutrition diagnosis at intake, anchored to her documented poverty.
Low and irregular income from writing, with a household to support; costs of care are a barrier
S — Synthetic social need anchored to her documented poverty and household responsibilities.
Acute uncomplicated cystitis, treated with nitrofurantoin rather than a fluoroquinolone during tuberculosis treatment; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated. First cervical screening done. Tdap, the first hepatitis B dose and the first HPV dose given. HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C screening were done at intake. [S]
Cervical cytology result by phone; repeat in three years if normal.
Hepatitis B dose 2 and HPV dose 2 at the end-of-treatment visit; HPV dose 3 six months after the first.
Influenza vaccine at the end-of-treatment visit.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Pulmonary tuberculosis, continuation phase (A15.0). Week 19 of 26 with no symptoms. Rifampin speeds the breakdown of the hormones in combined pills, patches, rings and implants and makes them unreliable. [S]
If she needs contraception during treatment or for four weeks after, a copper IUD, an injectable progestin or condoms are reliable.
Continue every dose; end-of-treatment visit after the 182nd dose.

Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition, improving (E44.0). Weight 42.6 kg from 38.5 kg at intake; BMI 19.4. [S]
Continue the meal plan and supplement drinks until her weight reaches 44 kg.

Low income (Z59.6). Public funding covers most tuberculosis costs; clinic charges are paid in instalments. [S]
Social worker to review her costs again at the end of treatment.

Guideline basis: Medicare Preventive Services reference: visit templates, screening cascades, and documentation elements (2026); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026); Cervical Cancer: Screening (2018); U.S. Selected Practice Recommendations for Contraceptive Use, 2024 (2024); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026)

Follow-up: End-of-treatment visit after the 182nd dose, with the chest X-ray, blood tests, the second hepatitis B and HPV doses and the influenza vaccine. Cytology result by phone. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1896-10-20: end-of-treatment review after 182 doses. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 16 minutes, with her consent. She understands that her tuberculosis is curable and wants full treatment of any illness. She named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and chose to record no other preferences today. To be revisited yearly. [S]
